question: In a TCS Prime (NQT 2026) technical round, after OOP and polymorphism questions and a statement that you practise DSA on LeetCode daily, the panel asked: **do you know any practical implementation of a linked list?** The reported answer was an LRU cache, explaining how a linked list and a hash map work together.
lookingFor: Can you tie a data structure to a real system rather than only reciting its definition?
Can you design an LRU cache with O(1) get and put and justify each component?
Do you understand why a doubly linked list (not a singly linked one) and why a hash map are both needed?
Can you list other practical uses of linked lists?
Can you handle follow-ups on eviction, capacity, and concurrency?
followUps: Why can't you use a singly linked list for the LRU cache?
How would you make the cache thread-safe without a single global lock?
How would you add per-entry time-to-live expiry?
How does LFU differ from LRU and how would you implement it in O(1)?
